loan.from: Ultimately Persian, via an unclear Eastern Iranic language

loan.form: kafa 'occupit, head'. Rum ceafă is a loan < Alb
capessere ~ capissere 'to seize, snatch at', or < Rom. *capsare based on Lat capere 'to take'. Either way, a loan
*rombulus based on Lat rhombus 'magic whirligig or wheel', or < Att Gk ρνμβος 'top, gyro; bell-clapper (clerical)
*manctus, based on Lat mancus 'maimed, infirm', cf also Ital manca 'left hand'
pinna, penna 'feather; pair of oxen'. Second meaning is a metaphoric derivative of the latter, meaning more 'plumage'
arēna id. Holm, however, prefers an alternative etymology < IE *er- 'sand, locker' (cf Lat rārus) but has no recent cognates
gola id (?), made obvious by variant golë
kafa 'occupit, head'. Poss. link with Lat. caput? Rum ceafă is an Albanian loanword!
milza id., possibly even earlier < Goth *milti (cf Cat melsa) 'milt, spleen'. Suppletion zeze 'black' follows Trk usage of colours for entrails, cf karaciger 'liver' with kara 'black'
*manctus, based on Lat mancus 'maimed, infirm', cf also Ital manca 'left hand'
